utterances.text: Could you just tell us what you see. This building -- let's start on the -- it's a broad, it's a broad photo; therefore, we have two pieces of it. If you start on the --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: This one that I'm pointing at is the Partizan Sports Hall, and this is the SUP building, the Foca police building, and this is the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas was pointing first on the building with the red roof on the right-hand side on the photo as Partizan, then to the white building in the middle of the photo as the SUP, and then to the left-hand side building --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: -- the municipality building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, why did you document this place?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: I wanted to show the close proximity of these buildings to the Partizan Sports Hall where victims were detained in this particular sports hall, and the victims that were detained there complained of alleged -- of mistreatment and rapes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you interview some of these detainees that were detained in Partizan?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The photos can be taken away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they tell you what happened to them in Partizan?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this was sometime ago now, the witnesses alleged that they were taken out of Partizan to other various places and they were raped. And this particular Partizan Sports Hall was not far from the SUP building. It was 113.5 metres, and whatever that was taken place, the witnesses alleged that could be seen from the police, police station, and they -- when they then reported this incident or incidents to the Foca SUP commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And you said you measured the -- you measured the distance between Partizan and the SUP building, which way did you measure? What did you measure exactly?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: From the entrance of the Partizan Sports Hall to the entrance of the SUP building, it took the pathway leading down, if you look through the pictures from 7308 to 7309, it measures -- 7308 to 7311 -- to 10. Go down to 7311, that will bring you to 113.5 metres as the distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, have you finished?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, why do we need this detail? I can understand that you want to refer to this subject matter as part of the attack upon the civilian population --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- for certain purposes, but do we really need this detail?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I was just -- I just wanted to mention that I don't want to show all these photos because I would like to refer you simply to the binder so you can look afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. But why do we need all this detail about how far it is from one building to the other?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Because the Prosecution thinks that it is very important to state here and to bring in evidence showing --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the speaker please slow down; the interpreters cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: To show that what happened in Partizan was well visible for the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But what does it prove in this case?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It proves the attack, that the attack on the Muslim population, was not -- nothing that occurred without the, the authorities knowing, just on the contrary. This is the central policy element.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I hope we're not going to have to spend too much time on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There's a very real issue as to whether you need to prove a policy, but I won't worry you about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can move on. This is actually the only question that I wanted to raise in relation to Partizan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, did you also go to the Foca High School?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you speak with the director of the Foca High School?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke to the director of the Foca High School, a Mr. Milenko Panic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: And he told me that the Serb -- non-Serb population were kept at the school for their own protection, and they were free to go whenever they wanted to leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask him for this information, or did he volunteer it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: No, he volunteered this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness now the photo 7332 of Exhibit 18.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please remember to pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That was obviously from one of the interpreters who has the same problem we've had throughout with everybody speaking the same language, so we must all comply with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, when you stood in front of the Foca High School and you looked onto the opposite side of the River Cehotina, onto which neighbourhood did you look?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: That would be the Cezluk [phoen] neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the photo now on the ELMO, is that what you saw?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes. I can identify it because of the Serb orthodox church, the same mukala [phoen] up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see any destruction in this neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: No. It looked strange. There was no destruction in that neighbourhood around the church.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. This photo can be removed from the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see destruction in other parts of the town?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. In the neighbourhood Aladza, Donje Polje, Gornje Polje, and the whole -- the old Foca town centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of neighbourhoods were these, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: From my knowledge, I think they were Muslim neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how could you know that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: From one of the photographs we have, when you see the destructions around it, I could say there's a mosque there, so I would say it's a Muslim neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we show the witness the photo 7290.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, could you point out the mosque, if there is any, on the photo.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: This is a very bad copy here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You'll have to have one of the microphones in your direction so that we can hear it.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Sorry. It's down there.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Ms. Manas was pointing on the -- right into the middle of the photo where there is destruction and a building with a round roof. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you document destructions in these neighbourhoods you just mentioned on a video?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Schouten did.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your permission, the Prosecution would like to show a brief video segments of these destructions and would then request it to be entered into evidence as Exhibit 410.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any objection to its admission into evidence, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P410.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And if we could ask to play it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we please see it, and could you please comment on what we see, Ms. Manas.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Well, this neighbourhood is around the Foca High School. As you can see, behind the school there was destruction of houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is still the Aladza neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. No, this is the -- this area is -- oh. This is the Aladza mosque area. The adjacent road is the Milica Osmana Djikica. As you can see, remnants of the grave sites.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Oh, no, it continues.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Further destruction around the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. You have already mentioned the Aladza mosque and where it was situated, and we saw it briefly in the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we now have the photo 7389.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that where the mosque was?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes. Plus you can see by the foundation which we found, remnants of the foundation and the site.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Did you ever get any photos showing what the Aladza mosque looked like when it was still standing?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes. Recently, in December 2000, the Office of the Prosecutor interviewed a historian, and he presented us with a book, "The Art in Herzegovina," in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there are some pictures in it which shows the Aladza mosque, what it looked like before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, these would now be new exhibits, and I suggest that we put it on the ELMO and we give it a new exhibit number, because they were not taken by the investigative team but are taken from the book just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Have they been shown to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: They have received a copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: This is the Aladza mosque before the destruction, which is taken from the book "The Art In Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you also have a photo from the interior which was also in the book?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please put it on the ELMO as well.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: This is the interior of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Would you please return to the photo of the interior just before this one. Ms. Manas, when you look at the bottom left-hand side, there is a pillar.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- according to the historian, he said it was a stalactite. And we, at a recent investigation done by the Bosnian State Commission in September, year 2000, a representative from the office of the OTP, Mr. Brian Strongman, and investigator Don King, they were observers to an excavation done by the Bosnian State Commission, and during the excavation they found various parts resembling the Aladza mosque and something of that in a photograph just taken by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We come to this later.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Okay. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I just want to draw the attention of the Court and the Defence to this particular feature on the photo. Your Honours, we have also prepared a short video sequence from the Aladza mosque when it was still standing, and it would -- we would like to show it and would like to have it entered into evidence as Exhibit 411. It's just a brief one- or two-minute video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Has the Defence seen that?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. They received the video as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objection, simply because we received the video copies only today.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We are watching it, Mr. Bakrac. The problem is we only produced it recently because we also received this only recently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I won't ask Mr. Bakrac whether he objects to it until after we have seen it and he has seen it. So you can express a view about its admissibility after you have seen it, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We couldn't do it earlier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, could you comment on what we see?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Now we're looking at the Aladza mosque, its exterior, minaret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us the date when this was made?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: From the video itself, it was made on the 18th April 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This round building, what was it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: That was the water fountain. You also find tombstones around the premises.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: There should be some -- there should be another sequence. Yes.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: This is the inside of the mosque. You have seen the pictures earlier. This is actually the ceiling of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the pillar you were talking about?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes. That's the stalactite and the stalagmite at the bottom. That's a pillar.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, now, Mr. Bakrac, have you any objection to that going into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I shall give you an answer if you allow me for a minute to consult with my client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That will be Exhibit P411.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, you showed us the empty space where this mosque was -- had been standing. Did you find the rubble of the mosque actually somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We found it opposite KP Dom on the river bank.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would now be the third video. We have a short video sequence of this rubble in front of the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We'll give Mr. Bakrac the opportunity and his client the opportunity of seeing it before I ask him whether he has any objection to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So it can be shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you again then comment on what we see, Ms. Manas.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: The building on the right is the KP Dom. This is the river bank of the Drina River. This is the rubble from the mosque. The only way we identify it is because of its marble structure and some ornamental designs on it. You can note the impressions, ornamental design, on the stone structure that you'll find inside the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: This was a kind of a grave. It resembled a kind of a grave, recently made. The camera is focused towards a boot. It was visibly seen, and a piece of clothing as well. Here you find a pillar, the outside of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you want to speak to your client, Mr. Bakrac, as to the admissibility of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Your Honour, the Defence is not denying the authenticity of the recording, of the time and place when it was made; however, the Defence cannot be certain that these parts that are being shown are indeed parts of the Aladza mosque, and it is in that sense that we do object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I don't think you're being asked to make that admission. All you're being asked to agree, that that is a video showing this rubble. Now, the witness has given certain evidence that parts of it are identifiable with the mosaics or particular decoration inside the mosque. There may be some other evidence or not, but it's up to us in the end to determine it. You're not being asked to admit it. If it's relevant in the case and the fact that the rubble outside the KP Dom happens to be that of some of the mosque that was destroyed, it's a matter for the Prosecution to prove. You are not being asked to admit that fact at the moment. You are only being asked to admit that that is a video -- or to agree to the admissibility of that video as something that was seen at the time that it was taken on the slopes of the river near the KP Dom. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I fully agree, but I thought it was necessary to object the way I did. But we do accept this material as authentic, and we agree that it can be admitted into evidence as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. And it has been noted on the transcript you don't admit the description given to it. That's perfectly all right. That will be Exhibit P412.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, do you have any recent photos from the same dump site?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes, we do. There were photos taken from an excavation site.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness these photos, and the Defence has copies of these photos.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we see here on this photo?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: According to the historian, he identified it as stalagmite or stalactite from the inside of the mosque because of the characteristic of the colours on the design here. Red was chiefly used inside the mosque, because no colours were used outside, so this would belong to the interior of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could the historian be sure that it was from the Aladza mosque?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: They viewed both the pictures, and from my understanding and from his interview, he had very good knowledge about the Aladza mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Aladza mosque the only mosque in Foca, according to this historian, which had such stone pillars?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Yes. The historian said that it was very unique because the Aladza mosque is the only mosque with such characteristic inside the mosque. You will never find this in any other mosque in eastern Europe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we see the next photo? What would this be?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: The historian identified as part of a pillar, the red - you can't see it on the - the red painting, which is also characteristic from the inside of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next photo, please, what is it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: This one was identified by the historian as a pillar from the exterior of the mosque which actually holds the pillars to the mosque itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for interrupting Ms. Manas, but I would kindly ask her to go more slowly through this material because it's difficult for us to follow the descriptions when the photographs are put on the monitor or, rather, on the ELMO so fast. We find it difficult to follow the description compared to what we see on the monitor. Perhaps someone can first tell us the number of the photograph so that we could get it ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That would also assist you so that when you have the transcript, you can compare the description with what you see on the photograph. But it's fair enough, I think. Let's have the number of the document, if there is one.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have not yet a number. We would -- it has an internal Prosecution numbering but, of course, not yet an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But for us to look at the transcript later with the photographs in front of us, it's essential that they have some identification --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, would you always tell us the number on the back side of the photo first, and then show us maybe a little bit longer this photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And I think that both Mr. Bakrac and the interpreters would like you to speak a little more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. I'll do so.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: The first picture, A34 [Realtime transcript read in error "834"], which is marked on the rear of the photograph, this represents the stalagmite inside the mosque. The historian identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sorry, your microphone is not on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: I shall repeat again. The first picture represents -- A34 represents a stalagmite from the interior of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise for interrupting again, but I heard in the interpretation 834, and on the photograph -- I mean, I heard 834, so I was just wondering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way the court reporter has it, but it was A34, I think, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: A34, A, alpha 34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, maybe I -- can I suggest something? We maybe give those photos ID numbers which later could be, if it is accepted, become the P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, the number on the back is sufficient identification, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: As I was saying, the unique colours on this pillar or stalactites, the red colour which was identified by the historian, which is very unique to the Aladza mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the next photo, what is the identification number?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Bravo 3. This is a pillar, also you can say it's a stalagmite or a stalactite. The historian identified as a pillar from the mosque because of the painting, as you would see on the right -- right at the bottom, some red painting on it. It's the only way he identified it as part of the mosque structure. Bravo 13, this is the pillar which was from the exterior of the mosque. The historian identified it by its metal ring because this actually held the structures in support.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And the last photo?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: Alpha 28. As you can see, this is a stone pillar that was taken which is also identified from the exterior of the Aladza mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, can you tell us, this photo, now we can see some people on the photo. When were these photos made, who made them, and why?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS
utterances.text: These photos were made on the 18th of September, as you can note - it's reflected on it - last year. The Bosnian State Commission for finding of missing persons conducted this excavation in order to exhume, maybe, corpses; and, of course, they exhumed this site and they found Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. rubbles. And from the office of the Prosecutor, the forensic project manager, Mr. Brian Strongman, and investigator, Don King, was present during the excavation as observers, and they made these photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution is in the position to present this historian as a witness, but we showed the photos through Ms. Manas to avoid to have another -- an expert here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, there was an awful lot of hearsay there, if I may say so --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- which may or may not be accepted. Perhaps you if you could have a discussion with counsel about whether they require you to produce the expert --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: -- and then you can resolve that problem before we proceed next week.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, but nevertheless, the Prosecution would like to enter these photos into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is there any objection to them being made exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How many photographs were there in all?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How many photographs were there in all?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Four. Oh, including the photographs from the book, it was altogether seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Seven. Well, those seven photographs will be Exhibit P413.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And they will bear after the numbers 413 the identifying reference on the back of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honour, it's now 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is indeed. We will resume next Monday at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
